features.name: capital_run_length_ratio
features.description: Ratio of the longest capital run length to the average capital run length, capturing bursts of capitalization relative to the typical run.
features.expected_model_benefit: Tree models can split on this ratio to isolate documents with unusually long, concentrated blocks of capital letters compared to their baseline.

features.name: total_special_char_freq
features.description: Sum of all character frequency features, representing the overall density of special characters in the text.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a single aggregate measure of special character usage, allowing trees to easily separate text with high overall symbol density.
features.formula: char_freq_0 + char_freq_1 + char_freq_2 + char_freq_3 + char_freq_4 + char_freq_5

features.name: high_capital_run_indicator
features.description: Boolean indicator for whether the longest capital run length exceeds 50 characters.
features.expected_model_benefit: Explicitly flags extreme capitalization, saving the tree model from having to find this specific threshold during early splits.

features.name: frequent_words_sum
features.description: Sum of the frequencies of several commonly occurring words (indices 18, 20, 24, 26) to capture a broader thematic presence.
features.expected_model_benefit: Aggregates related high-frequency word features, reducing dimensionality and providing a stronger, more stable signal for tree splits.

features.name: capital_run_length_total_log
features.description: Log-transformed total number of capital letters, compressing the long tail of the distribution.
features.expected_model_benefit: While trees are invariant to monotonic transformations, log-scaling can help stabilize variance and improve the resolution of splits in the lower range of values.

features.name: char_freq_3_exceeds_threshold
features.description: Indicator for whether char_freq_3 is greater than 0.5, capturing a significant presence of this specific character.
features.expected_model_benefit: Creates a hard categorical split for a feature with a highly skewed distribution, isolating extreme values directly.

features.name: word_freq_18_20_interaction
features.description: Multiplicative interaction between word_freq_18 and word_freq_20, highlighting documents where both words appear frequently together.
features.expected_model_benefit: Exposes a non-linear relationship between two high-frequency words that a tree model would otherwise need multiple splits to approximate.

features.name: capital_run_length_longest_log
features.expected_model_benefit: Compresses extreme outliers in the longest run length, potentially leading to more balanced and robust tree splits.

features.name: char_freq_4_5_sum
features.description: Sum of char_freq_4 and char_freq_5, combining two potentially related character frequency signals.
features.expected_model_benefit: Groups similar character features, allowing the model to split on their combined presence rather than relying on individual, weaker signals.

features.name: word_freq_24_26_max
features.description: The maximum value between word_freq_24 and word_freq_26, capturing the dominant frequency among these two words.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a single feature representing the strongest signal from a pair of related words, simplifying the decision boundary for the tree.

features.name: capital_density_proxy
features.description: Ratio of total capital letters to the longest run, indicating whether capitals are spread out or concentrated in a single block.
features.expected_model_benefit: Captures the structural distribution of capital letters, offering a novel interaction that trees can use to differentiate text formatting styles.

features.name: semantic_urgency_score
features.description: A semantic assessment of the text's urgency or aggressive tone, derived from the combination of high special character frequencies and long sequences of capital letters.
features.expected_model_benefit: Provides a high-level, interpretable score that synthesizes multiple low-level syntactic features into a single, powerful splitting criterion for tree models.
